pull_request.title: Documentation: Full tracker TDR review baseline
pull_request.head: codex/tracker-tdr-review-baseline
pull_request.body:
The TDR previously covered the pixel detector while the selected short- and long-strip assemblies remained only in design and validation records. The existing Overleaf report now has a full-tracker overview, detailed short/long-strip barrel and endcap sections, and a cross-subsystem review matrix. The 39-page edition is published to the user-authorized Overleaf main at `908e7e539d357738efe223a2d980ab2caa2e5144`.

Eight new vector drawings cover the nominal r–z layout, common service reservations, both strip barrels, short-stave construction, long-stave anchors/sag screening and both endcap petal systems. Tables distinguish complete strixels from separate stereo sensor faces, retain actual disc datums and describe the fixed service reservations. The new text explains local support, mounting, cooling, cabling, route transitions and conditional engineering calculations.

The existing pixel manuscript/data/drawings remain byte-identical. Bundled snapshots, deterministic figure generation and exact source/artifact/native-execution identities are retained in the TDR and [publication inventory](docs/publication/tracker-review-baseline.json). Source publication commits do not replace native execution hashes. The report keeps the coverage losses and failed/unqualified thermal, handling, guard and service-packing screens explicit.

This is a baseline for human technical review. DES019–023 remain DRAFT. The documentation PR is stacked on the merged subsystem prototype branch `codex/short-strip-endcap`; it does not independently integrate all strip compacts into production main or grant design sign-off.

Validation:

- Actual final Overleaf pdfLaTeX build: 39 A4 pages, zero errors/warnings/info; no box/LaTeX/undefined-reference diagnostics in the retained raw log. All final pages rendered and visually inspected.
- 23 pinned parent source hashes, nine generated artifacts and 29 preserved pixel files verified. Repeated figure generation was byte-identical.
- Logger: 121 valid paired records; current-turn counters unavailable and left unknown. Dashboard: 52 tasks, 29 documents, 19 review rounds; build passed.
- Full TDR source-relative and parent/main-relative whitespace checks passed. No scientific inputs, transforms, native evidence or engineering limits changed; no new native simulation run.

The publication receipt records the downloaded PDF SHA256 `d89ad510307aecc1c9ef6d772e9758377638cb8137c59b54ddf5156ef886d129` and distinguishes its optimized bytes from the compiler output. Private Overleaf URLs are omitted.

events.text:
Overleaf main now carries the 39-page tracker review edition at
`908e7e539d357738efe223a2d980ab2caa2e5144`. Eight vector figures cover the nominal
r–z layout, common service reservations, both strip barrels, local short stave,
long anchor schedule/sag screen, and both petal systems. Counts, measurement
frames, local supports, cooling, mounting, electrical routes, fixed service limits
and retained failure cases are described together.

Bundled snapshots and exact producer/source hashes make figure generation
self-contained. The long barrel uses a true retained-solid cut at z=166.50 mm;
short barrel and disc drawings explicitly project different depths. Twenty-nine
existing pixel manuscript/data/figure/table files remain byte-identical. Public
literature supports technological precedent, while project dimensions remain
explicit design choices. Publication hashes never replace native execution SHAs.

This is a coherent review layout, not a demonstrated integrated detector. Shared
service cells must be replaced once, standalone masses must not be added as a
full material budget, and coupled acceptance, global/joint mechanics, cold thermal
contacts, electronics, hydraulics, handling and service packing require review.
No sign-off, acceptance or scientific production integration is recorded.
